verdicts.flaw_description: "Rates cover every patient admitted to each ward, and a quarter of each ward's patients had spells outside the protocol." The measured population is not the exposed population: a quarter of the counted patients spent part of their stay off the protocol, so the infection rate mixes protocol and non-protocol person-time and the drop cannot be attributed to the handwashing protocol.

"Prey abundance on the surrounding farmland ran a third above the previous year's, and every box stood at the farmland edge, within the birds' foraging range." An uncontrolled confounder that plainly reaches the study units: food supply rose by a third in exactly the area the boxed birds foraged, which alone could explain the higher fledgling counts versus the previous spring.

"Readings cover every enrolled user in each cohort, and a fifth of each cohort used the app on some nights." Exposure is partial while the outcome is measured over everyone enrolled, so the heart-rate drop is computed on a population that was largely not (or only intermittently) using the app; the app cannot be credited with the change.

"Rates cover the boards soldered on the new profile throughout, and about a tenth of each run's boards took one pass on the old profile." About a tenth of each run is silently dropped from the defect rate, and those excluded boards are exactly the mixed-profile ones most likely to be reworked/defective, so the reported rate is a selectively favourable denominator rather than the run's true defect rate.

"Pass rates cover the students who attended every block, and about a quarter of each cohort missed at least one block." The pass rate is computed only on perfect attenders while a quarter of the cohort is excluded; attendance is self-selected and correlates with ability and motivation, so the 4-8 point gain over the previous term reflects who was counted, not the tutoring.
